title: Research Journal #40 — What the First Windows Stress Tests Could Tell Us
html:
Historical reconstruction of September 22, 2026

The evening before, we had results for all 30 BTLB-SIM architecture stress cases on macOS. Eight had exposed failures under the audit criteria. The other 22 passed locally, and each still needed native Windows evidence for a combined pass. Research Journal #39 ended at that point.

On September 22, the first native Windows run observed the same eight case-level failure patterns. It also raised a different question. When a test cannot reach the behavior it was designed to examine, what can we conclude from its output?

Checkpoint Ledger scope Pass Fail Inconclusive
September 21 evening macOS alone 22 8 0
September 21 evening Combined, with all Windows cases pending 0 8 22
September 22 initial return, v3 Combined, with native Windows evidence 18 8 4
September 22 targeted follow-up, v5 Combined, incorporating four native Windows rechecks 20 8 2

Each row accounts for the same 30 frozen cases. A combined pass required evidence from both platforms for the supported variants being assessed. The initial Windows run covered all 30 IDs, with some tests stopping before their intended checks. The follow-up ran four IDs and carried forward the other 26 dispositions. [1–3]

A test harness is the software surrounding a test that prepares its inputs, starts the operation being examined, collects its results, and evaluates those results against defined criteria. A problem in the harness can prevent us from learning whether the software under investigation behaves correctly. Before changing the software itself, we needed to determine which part of the system was responsible for the observed behavior.

Two checks that could finally finish

In case AR17-001, several worker processes tried to publish the same record. The first Windows run timed out in all 20 attempts and never established the corrupt-target variant. The follow-up isolated how the test collected results. In a separate diagnostic, five of eight Windows workers were still alive after reporting that they had queued their results. All eight exited normally once the test read the queue. With extra data in each message, all eight waited until the queue was read.

In effect, the test was waiting for the workers to finish while the workers could be waiting for the test to receive their results. Changing how those results were collected allowed the intended publication behavior to be examined without changing the production software or the audit criteria.

All 20 healthy-target and 20 corrupt-target checks passed. The diagnostic supports a result-collection explanation for the original timeouts. The exact scheduling of the original run remains unknown. [2, 3]

In case AR17-030, the VAPE archive verifier stopped before checking the archive because it could not import the software package. The WC verifier passed in the same run. The follow-up pointed the VAPE verifier to the bundled source, and it checked the unchanged archive successfully at both the opening and closing boundaries. The VAPE scope was 10 cases and 98 objects. The WC verifier checked 725 objects. The returned records report that the same 683 baseline files matched their expected hashes before and after both runs. [2, 3]

Two questions that stayed open

Case AR17-016 was designed to see how the engine handled different kinds of work when a deadline expired. The follow-up reached the variant in which a module continued working past its limit and confirmed that the engine rejected the overdue result. In the other variant, the run-wide 20-millisecond budget expired before the module entered. The test therefore still lacked native Windows evidence about how that module responds to the deadline while it is running. [2, 3]

Case AR17-029 hit a Windows permission restriction when the test tried to create symbolic links. Read-only and separate caller-owned path checks passed. The link-dependent checks remained incomplete under the available permissions, and the overall case stayed inconclusive. [2, 3]

An inconclusive result is not a pass, but neither does it necessarily establish a defect in the software being investigated. It identifies a question for which the available evidence is insufficient. Preserving that distinction prevents us from claiming more than our tests have actually demonstrated.

What the audit carried forward

The eight failing cases stayed in the ledger. Some exercised stronger criteria than the current software promised, and observing the same patterns on a second platform still left their causes and corrective obligations to be worked out. The original timeouts, the import error, the unreached test behavior, and the permission denial all remained part of the record. The combined total improved because two checks could finally produce usable evidence with the same production code and criteria.

At the September 22 checkpoint, discovery coverage remained incomplete. The results are internal software verification within the exercised scope. Architecture acceptance, independent scientific reproduction, and physical evidence remained outside what these runs established. The later Research Records #1 records how the investigation eventually closed with unresolved obligations.

Sources

  1. Beyond the Light Barrier, AR-1.7 Discovery Summary and 30-case ledger v2. Frozen audit specification 51e6d4cfe1e5b906b0691df006205160a4184f5d, baseline 2e3af1d33012c15110d470f3619eafc5ecf2f982.
  2. Beyond the Light Barrier, AR-1.7 Discovery Summary v3 — native Windows return reviewed, v3 dispositions and boundary integrity record, and native return run-20260922-133547-ed97bd, September 22, 2026.
  3. Beyond the Light Barrier, AR-1.7 Discovery Summary v4 — four-case follow-up, R2 harness revision record, and AR-1.7 Discovery Summary v5 — Windows R2 reviewed, v5 dispositions and boundary integrity record, and native return run-20260922-185231-95e556, September 22, 2026. These internal source identities identify the evidence underlying the article.

The supporting evidence package contains selected records from the original Windows return and the four-case follow-up, including the case dispositions, harness controls, and archive verification excerpts. It does not provide a complete executable reproduction or establish independent reproduction.
